title: Tokyo: From a castle to the clouds
audience: Curious beginners who may know nothing about Japan.
runtimeNote: m3 is a short historical bridge into m4, together forming the Tokyo Tower learning section. Preserve that bridge before the timeline tests 1868.

modules.title: From a castle to the clouds.
modules.body:
How does a castle town become a city of giant towers?

Welcome to Tokyo, Japan’s capital—once called Edo. Its story reaches back to 1457, when the warrior Ōta Dōkan built a castle here.
modules.imageAlt: Illustrated Edo castle town beside a moat

modules.title: A ruler makes his home.
modules.body:
Tokugawa Ieyasu made Edo Castle his home in 1590. In 1603, he established his government as shogun—Japan’s military ruler.

The emperor remained in Kyoto. Around Edo’s government, a growing city needed homes, shops, streets, and aqueducts to carry water.

modules.title: A new name. A growing city.
modules.body:
In 1868, Edo became Tokyo, meaning “Eastern Capital.” Emperor Meiji established his residence here the following year.

Today, different neighborhoods reveal different sides of Tokyo: Asakusa’s temples and traditional shops, Akihabara’s electronics and anime—Japanese animation—and Shibuya’s shopping and nightlife.
modules.imageAlt: Illustrated map of Japan introducing Tokyo with Mepamo-kun

modules.title: Look up.
modules.body:
Completed in 1958, Tokyo Tower stands 333 meters tall. It helped send television signals across the city and became a symbol of Japan’s postwar recovery.

Its distinctive international orange and white colors help make it visible to aircraft.
modules.imageAlt: Orange-and-white Tokyo Tower above city buildings

modules.title: A skyline with a purpose.
modules.body:
As buildings grew taller, they could interfere with broadcasts. Tokyo Skytree opened in 2012, reaching 634 meters—almost twice Tokyo Tower’s height.

It helps signals reach beyond surrounding high-rises, while observation decks give visitors sweeping views.

A castle helped shape the city. Towers helped connect it.
modules.imageAlt: Pale Tokyo Skytree above the city

quizzes.title: Complete the sentence.
quizzes.instruction: Tap a word to fill the blank.
quizzes.sentenceBefore: Before it was called Tokyo, the city was known as

incorrectFeedback.title: A little clarification.
incorrectFeedback.body: The city was called Edo before it became Tokyo.

options.text: A military ruler called a shogun
An emperor who lived in Kyoto
A merchant who sold goods in Edo

correctFeedback.title: Exactly!
correctFeedback.body: Ieyasu was a shogun. He governed from Edo, while the emperor remained in Kyoto.

incorrectFeedback.title: A little clarification.
incorrectFeedback.body: Ieyasu was a shogun—a military ruler. The emperor was a different person, living in Kyoto.

quizzes.title: What did Tokyo Tower help bring to people’s homes?

correctFeedback.title: Exactly!
correctFeedback.body: Tokyo Tower broadcast television signals across the city, helping people watch programs at home.

incorrectFeedback.title: A little clarification.
incorrectFeedback.body: Tokyo Tower helped broadcast television signals. It did not supply water or electricity to homes.

quizzes.title: Why did Tokyo need a taller broadcasting tower?
quizzes.imageAlt: Illustrated Tokyo Skytree rising above nearby buildings

options.text: Nearby high-rises could interfere with television broadcasts.
Tokyo Tower had stopped attracting visitors.
Television signals needed to travel underground.

correctFeedback.title: Exactly!
correctFeedback.body: Skytree’s greater height helps broadcast signals clear nearby buildings and reach more homes.

incorrectFeedback.title: A little clarification.
incorrectFeedback.body: Nearby high-rises could interfere with television broadcasts. Skytree’s greater height helps signals clear those buildings.

quizzes.title: Put Tokyo’s story in order.
quizzes.instruction: Tap the events from earliest to latest.

correctFeedback.title: You’ve connected the story!
correctFeedback.body: Edo became Tokyo in 1868. Tokyo Tower followed in 1958, and Skytree opened in 2012 as broadcasting needs changed.

incorrectFeedback.title: Here’s how the story unfolded.
incorrectFeedback.body: First, Edo was renamed Tokyo in 1868. Tokyo Tower was completed in 1958. Skytree opened in 2012.

complete.title: Now the skyline has a story.
complete.body: A castle helped shape the city. Towers helped connect it.
